newsitem.title: USA: Most stock index futures begin weaker with T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: Most stock index futures begin weaker with T-bonds.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures began the session weak, in line with losses in U.S. Treasury bond futures.
Traders said a weak T-bond tone and worries of profit taking to recent sharp gains kept buyers nervous.
"With bonds weak, I think we could see a little pullback today," an S&P 500 futures trader said.

As June T-bonds slipped to a new session low, so did June S&Ps, eroding through support at 829.80 and 829.30. Tuesday's session low of 827.70 was considered minor support, with major support was pegged at 823.75 to 824.00.

Preliminary 1997 first-quarter productivity data ushered June T-bonds to their session low. Unit labor costs rose 2.7 percent while productivity was up 2.0 percent for the biggest gain since fourth-quarter 1993.
June S&P 500 futures slipped as low as 827.00, the lowest price since Friday. But traders and analysts said the market has rallied again to record highs rather quickly, and was due to consolidate.
"We're going to give back some of what we picked up," one S&P 500 futures trader said. He put support at 823.30, a launching point on Monday's rally.

Some technicians said the overall S&P 500 tone was firm. Monday, the contract set a new record high of 838.00 on brisk volume and a rise in open interest. In overnight trade Tuesday, June set another high at 838.40.
Since June S&Ps bottomed April 14 at 738.25, the contract has gained more than 100 points from that low to the record high.

At 0932 CDT/1432 GMT, June S&P 500s were down 6.25 points at 828.60, Value Lines lost 3.20 to 729.30, Nikkei fell 170.0 to 19,955.0, Russell lost 0.80 to 363.10, and NASDAQ rose 2.00 to 926.50. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
